properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 29 at 5:29PM CDT until August 30 at 9:10AM CDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following river in Illinois...
Indiana...

Wabash River at Hutsonville to Vincennes

.Minor flooding continues on the Wabash River from Hutsonville down
to Vincennes. The river has crested. Flooding should come to an end
on the Wabash over the weekend.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at Vincennes.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Considerable agricultural flooding extends
from just north of the junction of Illinois 33 with Business 50 to
the St. Francesville, Illinois area.  River Road from Lincoln
Memorial Bridge to Billett Rd is impassable.  Extensive seep water
forms behind Illinois levees extending from Russellville to U.S.
Highway 50.  Flooding of agricultural land begins in Knox County
Indiana west of the railroad extending for the Oaktown area to the
north side of Vincennes.  Extensive flooding of Small Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:45 PM CDT /5:45 PM EDT/ Saturday the stage was 16.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:45 PM CDT /5:45 PM EDT/ Saturday was 17.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this evening and continue falling to 4.4 feet Tuesday, September
08.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 915 AM CDT /1015
AM EDT/.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 29 at 8:36PM MST until August 29 at 11:15PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Pima County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 1115 PM MST.

* At 836 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Vamori, Cowlic, Choulic and Coldfields.

This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...
Indian Route 20 at Cowlic.

Significant rain has occurred on the western slopes of the
Boboquivari Mountains into the lower deserts from Topawa to the
International Border. Expect significant and rapid rises on washes
including the Vamori Wash. This will take some time for the flood
wave to move down the wash, which will likely occur after midnight.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 11:15 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 11:15 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 29 at 10:27PM MST until August 30 at 12:45AM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Western Graham County in southeastern Arizona...
East Central Pinal County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 1245 AM MST.

* At 1027 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms produced heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1
and 3 inches of rain have fallen in the Aravaipa Watershed.
Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected. A stream gauge in the Aravaipa Canyon showed a rapid 6
foot rise and this flood wave is moving downstream. Hikers and
campers should move away from the creek now.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Aravaipa Canyon Wilderness.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Deer Creek, Telegraph Wash and Aravaipa Creek.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 30 at 12:39AM CDT until August 30 at 1:45AM CDT by NWS Aberdeen SD
properties.description:
SVRABR

The National Weather Service in Aberdeen has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northeastern Sully County in central South Dakota...
East Central Dewey County in north central South Dakota...
Potter County in north central South Dakota...

* Until 145 AM CDT /1245 AM MDT/.

* At 1239 AM CDT /1139 PM MDT/, a severe thunderstorm was located
over Whitlocks Bay Rec Area, or 13 miles west of Gettysburg, moving
east at 25 mph.

THIS IS A DESTRUCTIVE STORM FOR SOUTHEAST POTTER COUNTY.

HAZARD...Three inch hail and 60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be severely injured.
Expect shattered windows, extensive damage to roofs,
siding, and vehicles.

* This severe thunderstorm will be near...
Whitlocks Bay Rec Area and Swiftbird around 1240 AM CDT.
Gorman around 1250 AM CDT.
Gettysburg around 110 AM CDT.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter now inside an interior room on the lowest floor of a
well-built structure. This storm is capable of producing destructive
hail and damaging winds.

Report severe weather to your nearest law enforcement agency or the
National Weather Service office in Aberdeen SD.

CMAMtext: NWS:DESTRUCTIVE HAIL STORM in this area til 145 AM CDT. Take shelter now. Check media.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WARNING in effect for this area until 1:45 AM CDT for DESTRUCTIVE three inch size hail. Take shelter in a sturdy building, away from windows. People and animals outdoors will be severely injured.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 29 at 5:22PM MST until August 30 at 12:15AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...the Colorado River near
mile marker 62.

* Until 1215 AM MST /115 AM MDT/ Tonight.

* At 522 PM MST /622 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
that produced heavy rain earlier southwest of Cameron have resulted
in a flash flood along the Little Colorado River west of Cameron.
Between 1 and 2 inches were estimate by radar earlier in the
afternoon. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
The flood wave is expected to reach the Colorado River between 10
PM and 1 AM.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain from
thunderstorms earlier.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding along the Little Colorado
River west of Cameron.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Little Colorado River Navajo Tribal Park.

This includes the following highways...
the Colorado River near mile marker 62. State Route 64 between mile
markers 281 and 284.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Blue Water Base Camp, Old Fish Camp Site, Above LCR Camp Site and
Below LCR Camp Site.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Blue Water Base Camp.

This includes the following Little Colorado River west of Cameron.
properties.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.
